audit_metadata.phase: Phase 7H-A — Metric, Normalization, and Provenance Verification
audit_metadata.objective: Reconcile decision rules, separate binary alert from 3-class prediction, and correct mislabeled Critical Recall

binary_failure_alert.interpretation: Flags whether ANY failure alert should be dispatched to operators.

three_class_prediction_rules.cascaded_threshold_rule: If P(Critical) >= theta_crit, assign 2. Else if P(Warning) + P(Critical) >= theta_fail, assign 1. Else assign 0. Disentangles urgency tier from alert threshold.
three_class_prediction_rules.argmax_among_alerts: If P(Warning) + P(Critical) >= theta: assign 2 if P(Critical) > P(Warning) else assign 1. Else assign 0.

episode_detection.rule: An episode is detected if AT LEAST ONE window within (0, 1800s] triggers a failure alert (y_pred > 0).
episode_detection.lead_time: Time from earliest alert in the episode to failure: t_fail - t_first_alert.

critical_class_window_recall.definition: Proportion of true Critical windows (y_true == 2) predicted specifically as Critical (y_pred == 2).
critical_class_window_recall.mislabeling_in_phase7h: In Phase 7H Section 7, the column labeled "Crit. Recall" in the threshold sweep was actually computed as the proportion of Critical windows where P(Warning) + P(Critical) >= theta. This is Binary Critical Interception Rate (P(alert | Critical)), NOT genuine 3-class Critical Recall (P(y_pred=2 | y_true=2)). Under the binary threshold rule, genuine class 2 is never predicted.
